prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "dalle", with the standing line "A pipeline that turns one seed address into a reproducible prompt, image, caption, and full artifact trail." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows A long horizontal ribbon printed with a hexadecimal seed address, mirrored and joined to itself at the left. Small windows six characters wide are cut from the ribbon at regular intervals; each window drops on a thin line into one drawer of a low card cabinet whose fifteen drawers are labelled with word lists. One card lifts from each drawer and the cards gather at the right into a stack of written prompt sheets, which feed a single square canvas on an easel. A caption bar sits across the canvas foot.

Magnified circles set beside it show A magnified circle on one six-character window showing the number it becomes and the drawer row it points at. A magnified circle on the caption bar showing three sampled colours averaged into a background with light or dark text chosen against it. A magnified circle on a finished canvas already in the folder, showing the run stopping early because the file exists.

Colour is used so that One accent marks the deterministic path from seed to prompt. A second accent marks the three calls that leave the machine. A third accent marks work skipped or reused from disk.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: fifteen attribute lookups drawn as fifteen drawers; six characters per window shown as a dimension mark on the ribbon; eight phases counted along the row of studies; nine output folders counted in the group at lower right; three sampled colours in the caption circle.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: series, seed, attribute, prompt, terse, enhanced, selector, annotated, generated, audio, adjectives, nouns, emotions, occupations, actions, adverbs, artstyles, litstyles, colors, gazes, backstyles, orientations, setup, image_wait, annotate, cache hit, dall-e-3 — each printed on the drawer, folder, step, or file it names.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: seed address, reverse and join, six hex window, adjectives, nouns, emotions, occupations, artstyles, litstyles, colors, backstyles, dall-e-3 index by modulo, contrast banner, cache hit setup, image_wait, annotate, series filter, context cache generated/, annotated/, selector/, enhanced/, terse, audio same seed, same art, no key, no call

Set these short notes beside what they explain: Each window picks one row, never random; Empty filter means the whole list stays Averaged palette decides the caption background; Existing file ends the run immediately Phase averages give percent and remaining time; Filters narrow a list by substring Every layer of prompt is kept; Caption text is burned into the copy Without a key, placeholders are written
